E013-01.notes: Present-perfect 'has changed' matches 'has crossed' and the parallel 'Its schedule, however, has not'; past perfect has no earlier past reference point. Needs the cue from the next sentence.

flags: minor: ship name 'Marguerite' would normally be italicized in a published passage; harmless here
E013-02.notes: Nonessential appositive renaming 'the current one' opens with a comma, so it must close with a comma; semicolon/dash/no punctuation break the pairing.

E013-03.notes: Inverted sentence: the subject is the compound list (nurses, cooks, a baker), so plural 'are'. C keeps singular 'is'; D produces a fragment.

E013-04.notes: 'depends on' needs the preposition; object of the preposition takes 'whom'; 'which' is wrong for a person (the baker); C drops 'on'.

E013-05.notes: Faulty comparison: 'Running a ferry at night' must be compared with an activity, 'running one during the day'. B compares the activity to a ferry; C to 'the day's' (nothing); A to 'daytime'.

E013-06.notes: Redundancy: 'at night when it is dark' repeats the context ('Running a ferry at night'). B is concise; C and D keep the redundancy.

E013-07.notes: Cause and effect: fog and hard-to-see buoys are why he memorized the channel. Contrast and similarity transitions don't fit.

E013-08.notes: No punctuation between the verb 'argued' and its 'that'-clause object.

flags: minor: D 'changed its directions' is unidiomatic as well as wrong, so it's an easy elimination
E013-09.notes: 'Reversed course' is the idiomatic figurative phrase for a policy reversal; B and C read literally or informally and are wrong for a city council.

flags: minor: A also echoes paragraph 1 (the 'eleven' departure), but only B picks up the ninety-year history and the 'dependable as the tide' idea, so B is clearly best
minor: B is the longest choice and repeats the key phrase word for word, which is a test-wise tell
E013-10.notes: B ties the ferry's survival back to the opening's ninety-year history and the 'as dependable as the tide' line. C and D bring in new topics.
